overclaims: OpenAI reports Python-related gains for two contemporary reasoning models, and the puzzle study documents successful tool-assisted execution where text-only attempts failed.
These results establish useful improvements on the kinds of tasks Marcus discusses.
checks.note: e1 gives only Python-enabled AIME scores (99.5%, 98.4%) and no tool-free baseline. Its quoted sentence is about tool use in general for visual and multi-step tasks, so calling these 'Python-related gains' goes beyond the evidence. Only e2 is a fixed-model with/without-tool comparison (one model, one puzzle family), and the payload's own limitations call it limited. 'Establish' is too strong for one limited study plus company-reported scores. Axis, horizon and outcome match the reviews. Excerpt and conditions are fine.

The rationale and limitations are supported by e1 (SimpleQA/PersonQA hallucination rates) and e2 (hallucinations found in testing of roughly final Claude 4 models; mitigation of one pattern incomplete), and they are suitably hedged. Citation error: the e2 locator says 'Section 4.2.2, Whole-model testing exercise', but the source heading is '4.2.2 Company-wide model testing exercise'. Correct the section title (page 46 is right). Excerpts, publishers, dates and relations are otherwise correct, and the outcome matches the reviews.
